# expm1relf

> Compute the relative error exponential of a single-precision floating-point number.

<!-- Section to include introductory text. Make sure to keep an empty line after the intro `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="intro">

The relative error exponential is defined as

<!-- <equation class="equation" label="eq:relative_error_exponential" align="center" raw="f(x) = \frac{e^x - 1}{x}" alt="Equation for the relative error exponential."> -->

```math
f(x) = \frac{e^x - 1}{x}
```

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<!-- Package usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```javascript
var expm1relf = require( '@stdlib/math/base/special/expm1relf' );
```

#### expm1relf( x )

Computes the relative error exponential of a single-precision floating-point number `x`.

```javascript
var v = expm1relf( 0.0 );
// returns 1.0

v = expm1relf( 1.0 );
// returns ~1.718

v = expm1relf( -1.0 );
// returns ~0.632

v = expm1relf( NaN );
// returns NaN
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<!-- Package usage notes. Make sure to keep an empty line after the `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   When `x` is near zero, `exp(x)-1` can suffer catastrophic cancellation (i.e., a significant loss in precision). `expm1relf` avoids such a loss in precision.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<!-- Package usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

<!-- eslint no-undef: "error" -->

```javascript
var uniform = require( '@stdlib/random/array/uniform' );
var logEachMap = require( '@stdlib/console/log-each-map' );
var expm1relf = require( '@stdlib/math/base/special/expm1relf' );

var opts = {
    'dtype': 'float32'
};
var x = uniform( 100, -50.0, 50.0, opts );

logEachMap( '(e^%0.3f - 1)/%0.3f = %0.3f', x, x, expm1relf );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<!-- C usage documentation. -->

<section class="usage">

### Usage

```c
#include "stdlib/math/base/special/expm1relf.h"
```

#### stdlib_base_expm1relf( x )

Computes the relative error exponential of a single-precision floating-point number.

```c
float out = stdlib_base_expm1relf( 0.0f );
// returns 1.0f

out = stdlib_base_expm1relf( 1.0f );
// returns ~1.718f
```

The function accepts the following arguments:

-   **x**: `[in] float` input value.

```c
float stdlib_base_expm1relf( const float x );
```

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<!-- C API usage notes. Make sure to keep an empty line after the `section` element and another before the `/section` close. -->

<section class="notes">

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<!-- C API usage examples. -->

<section class="examples">

### Examples

```c
#include "stdlib/math/base/special/expm1relf.h"
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>

int main( void ) {
    float x;
    float v;
    int i;

    for ( i = 0; i < 100; i++ ) {
        x = ( ( (float)rand() / (float)RAND_MAX ) * 100.0f ) - 50.0f;
        v = stdlib_base_expm1relf( x );
        printf( "(e^%f - 1)/%f = %f\n", x, x, v );
    }
}
```

</section>
